core: Political power, institutions and political thought
Empirical quantitative and qualitative political inquiry
questions: How do political institutions organise power?
How can evidence support political explanations and decisions?

trace: Introduces legal institutions, the role of law in society and constitutional and administrative concepts.
Examines political authority, justice, ideologies and normative arguments about the welfare state.
Compares regimes, parties, representation, constitutions, bureaucracies and policymaking institutions.
Introduces incentives, markets and aggregate outcomes as foundations for economic policy.
Develops survey design, operationalisation, sampling, research design and statistical inference.
Compares legislatures, executives, courts, constitutional rights and administrative remedies.
Explains interactions between states and non-state actors through competing international-relations theories.
Traces political ideologies and the development of democracy and dictatorship in modern history.
Adds sociological concepts for understanding inequality, group identities and social institutions.
Develops rhetorical analysis and argumentation, including deliberative speech and delivery.
Actual data cleaning, integration, visualisation and exploratory analysis supplies concrete empirical tools, without a guaranteed political/security dataset or dedicated big-data infrastructure.
Studies public provision, welfare programmes, social insurance, taxation and redistribution.
Analyzes market power, externalities and the rationale for government intervention.
Studies EU competences, rights, citizenship and enforcement of EU law.
Analyzes public policymaking across levels and develops policy memos through a substantive case.
Analyzes EU institutions, interest representation, legislative decision-making and implementation.
Explains open-economy policy, employment and fiscal and monetary choices.
Examines persuasion, framing, argument and communication ethics.
Actual prediction, model selection and validation supplies concrete empirical tools, without a guaranteed political/security dataset or dedicated big-data infrastructure.
Uses regression, instrumental variables and inference to assess causal and predictive claims.
Explores treaties, jurisdiction, international institutions and how domestic courts interact with international law.
Develops interviews, observation, coding and qualitative interpretation with attention to research ethics.

Description-only: question formulation, source criticism and substantial historical research in the American Century. It is historical inquiry, not a dedicated political-science or Dutch/global-politics project.
Uses register, point of view, modality and language choices to examine how discourse constructs meaning.
Examines algorithmic fairness, democratic implications and accountability; complements the evaluation of AI in public communication.
Actual television/digital storytelling, representation and power, with American and marginalisation cases, supports critical media interpretation. It is not Dutch politics or campaign-media research.
Develops analysis of audiovisual form and representation across film, television and platforms.
Adds normative analysis of social contracts, consequentialism and care ethics to public argument.

alternatives.label: Comparative politics and public policy
alternatives.concept: Study comparative political institutions, constitutional law, European governance and public economics. Investigate policy questions with quantitative and qualitative methods, supported by international relations and historical inquiry. UCR supplies broader comparative and European inquiry, rather than a dedicated Dutch national-institutional sequence or the two VU political research projects.
alternatives.labelReason: Actual disciplinary study and specific contributions sustain the bounded concept; no Dutch specialist sequence, full political-science training or identical thesis is claimed.
alternatives.distinctness: Five substitutions shift from extra data/international/historical inquiry toward actual stylistics, AI ethics, media interpretation and ethical argument, while retaining comparative politics, law, economics and research.
progression: All covered offerings/formal earlier prerequisites checked against unchanged current workbook. PPD is in year one; statistical and law foundations precede dependents.

alternatives.label: Political communication and public debate
alternatives.concept: A programme studying public argument through rhetoric, stylistics, media interpretation, persuasion, policy writing and AI ethics, anchored in comparative politics, constitutional/EU law and empirical inquiry. Television/media cases retain their actual cultural and American focus; they are not relabelled Dutch political communication or an established VU media specialisation.

routeSelection.route: Dutch-language National Politics and Government route
routeSelection.basis: Registry resolution case rc-0074 (normalization status step2-resolved-split) explicitly identifies cp-000113 as the Dutch-taught 'Nationale Politiek en Bestuur' track/version of the shared VU Political Science registration, distinct from the English 'Global Politics' track (cp-000112); the registry's own targets metadata records {"language":"NLD","focus":"national politics and governance"} for this exact target. OER Article 10.2 confirms that, starting cohort 2025-2026, the bachelor's programme (RIO 56606) offers exactly two named tracks -- 'Politicologie: Nationale Politiek en Bestuur' (Dutch) and 'Political Science: Global Politics' (English) -- so the normalized target itself names this exact official route (Section 2.1 rule 1), confirmed by current official evidence for the 2026-2027 academic year and by the Dutch-language 'politicologie' curriculum, overview and future/career webpages themselves, and by Article 10.4's confirmation that Dutch is the track's language of instruction.

selection.assessment: Two independently assessed feasible, meaningfully distinct programmes pass for the confirmed core. All eligible generators are owned by the comparative/public-policy core or the separately assessed media/AI-writing/debate option. Other current issues and careers remain support/search evidence, not additional generators.

blocks: Both examine political thought, authority and normative arguments; the precise syllabus differs.
Both compare political regimes, institutions and supranational/national political systems; UCR does not supply a dedicated Dutch case sequence.
Both concern constitutional institutions, democracy and the rule of law. UCR compares several systems; it does not reproduce the Dutch institutional emphasis.
Both address European politics and institutions; UCR does not reproduce the dedicated Netherlands-in-Europe viewpoint.
Both study relations among states and other actors; UCR uses international-relations theories, cases and a UN simulation.
Both concern government and economic intervention. UCR develops public goods, expenditure, taxation and redistribution rather than the complete VU economy/market/government syllabus.
Both develop empirical research design and measurement; UCR combines survey/experimental design and statistics in broader social science.
Both develop qualitative inquiry through actual research methods; UCR includes interviews/coding/reflexivity, with no identical political-project claim.

notes.text: UCR offers broader political, legal, economic and empirical inquiry. It does not reproduce the two dedicated VU political research projects, the full political-methods sequence or the required final political-science thesis. Dutch institutions, public management and the Netherlands-specific sequence receive less dedicated treatment. Media/communication courses retain their actual broader and American contexts.

audience.programmeDescription: National Politics and Governance studies Dutch public institutions, democracy, public management, economic policy and the Netherlands in Europe, with comparative and empirical political inquiry.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The confirmed comparative national politics and public governance and empirical-methods core supports two meaningful broader UCR responses, while the revised-cohort final-year theory and research culmination remains outside the assessed scope. UCR supplies sustained political/institutional and empirical study with the option-specific emphases shown. Dedicated VU projects and the final thesis are not reproduced; a complete external progression pathway is not certified.
